title: Power Apps: Power Apps CLI commands to find connectors and create connections for code apps
summary: The commands, licensing alternatives and administration paths are supported. Hold the briefing because its cost rationale says Microsoft documents no charge for the CLI commands, whereas the sources establish only that no CLI-specific charge is documented.

claims.claim: Power Apps adds CLI commands for developers to discover connectors and create connections for code apps.
claims.quote: The Power Apps CLI adds new commands that let developers discover available connectors and create connections directly from the command line.

claims.fix: Replace the cost rationale with: 'Low. No CLI-specific licence or meter is documented at the time of writing (November 2026); the known incremental cost is developer and admin time. Existing code-app licensing requirements still apply.' This preserves the distinction between an undocumented charge and a documented absence of charge.

claims.fix: The After rollout step on reviewing and removing connections names a control not represented in the table. Remove that checklist bullet if retaining the current two-row table.

claims.claim: Blockable connectors placed in a data policy's Blocked group cannot be used where that policy applies.
claims.quote: Blocked connectors can't be used where this policy is applied. Unblockable connectors are in Non-business by default.

claims.claim: Data policies control which connectors can be combined by separating them into data groups.
claims.quote: Connectors can reside in only one data group at a time. By moving the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors to the Business data group, you're preventing users from creating flows and apps that combine these two connectors with any of the connectors in the Non-business or Blocked groups.
